_about: How the Magic Portals port carries a traveller through a portal. Enhanced's
portals.json has a transit block, and marks every field of it _guess; this is the
original's rule, decoded from its compiled script, and it replaces that block. See

_source: The original's android_game.bin, decoded. PortalManager::teleportToOther
(PortalManager.angelscript, bytes 144944..145873) puts the traveller at its partner
portal's own position, SetPositionXY(other.GetPositionXY()), with no offset, and then
calls invertLinearVelocity (Portal.angelscript, bytes 360172..360571). That multiplies
a body's velocity by -1, and a character's by (1, -1): the character keeps its x and
turns its y back. There is no speed scale.
_lockout_note: Kept from Enhanced's portals.json, where it is a _guess. Nothing in teleportToOther

inside its exit does not go back until it has left, and this lockout covers the tick

_source: NOTHING GOES THROUGH A PLACED PAIR WHILE A MOVING PLATFORM OR A LIFT IS AT ANY PLACED
PORTAL. Decoded (planning step 136; listing out/parity/asbc/all_functions.txt, md5 48fe65ce).
PortalManager::teleportToOther (bytes 144944..145873) #36-42 calls
hasMovingPlatformInAnyPortal and returns, teleporting nothing, when it is true: after
mayTeleport (#25-35) and before isActive (#43-50). It is the ONE caller (a byte search), so
only the placed pair is gated: doTeleporting reaches teleportToOther when maxPortals is 2
(#33-120) and teleportToFirstStaticPortal when it is 1 (#121-144), and ETHCallback_portal_static
has its own path; neither of those two asks.
hasMovingPlatformInAnyPortal (bytes 147042..147305): for every entity in PortalManager.portals
(the placed ones), EntityGrabber(portal.GetPositionXY(), portalCollisionRadius x 0.4,
isMovingPlatform) (#7-29, arguments pushed last-first); any grab of size above 0 answers true
(#31-40). portalCollisionRadius is placement.json's entry_radius_px, 14 x getScale, so
radius_share 0.4 gives 5.6 units.
isMovingPlatform (MovingPlatforms.angelscript, bytes 372140..372382) is
GetEntityName() == 'moving_platform' || 'lift' || 'lift.ent', compared exactly: so
moving_platform_single.ent (inert, docs/original-gameplay.md section 6) is not one.
EntityGrabber::EntityGrabber (bytes 23924..24990), for these entities (shape 3, a polygon, so
not the circle branch #65-124): #126-194 Shape(GetPositionXY(), GetCollisionBox().size x
getScale(), GetAngle(), edgePlanes true).overlapSphere(point, radius). The box is the entity's
collision box as stored (64 x 32 for every moving_platform but one of 64 x 64 on level11c,
62 x 32 for every lift), CENTRED ON THE ENTITY'S POINT, not times its own scale.
The grabber takes its candidates only from the point's bucket and its neighbours (#16-23:
GetBucket, getEntitiesFromNeighbourBuckets); at the game's 128-unit bucket that holds every
body the box test could take (a grabbed body's centre is at most about 51 units from the
portal's point: half the 64 x 64 box's diagonal plus 5.6), so the port does not model it.
Shape::Shape (bytes 89202..91621) gives it its four sides and, with edgePlanes, four
45-degree planes through its corners (normals normalize(+-1, +-1) inward, not turned with the
angle); the two-argument Shape::overlapSphere (bytes 93178..93477) answers false as soon as
one plane's dot is at or below -radius. So, with a and b how far the portal's point lies past
the box's sides in x and y: held while a < r, b < r and a + b < r x sqrt(2).
The port looks for the entities named here, by the node's own shape bounds (none of the 29
in the game is turned or scaled, and Portals::Find refuses one that is).
